rows: Right, I rehearsed this speech three times and forgot two lines. Let me try the honest version.
I can brawl. Not my favourite thing, but I can do it when someone asks me.
Risk? I take them. I am tired of waiting for permission to try.
Slow is fine, I need that today. Sometimes I need to slow down to be sure I am here.
The people are why I keep turning up. They deserve more than a spare.
I am here, and I am glad to be.
I am not the headline, but I think I earn my place on the card.
Watch the stance. I worked on it. Nobody told me to stand this way.
Technique, you call it, and I will try mine. Show me one and I will try to match it, honestly.
Strikes hurt. I know that, and I would rather you did not test it on me.
Risk does not always pay off. I have seen that happen many times.
Stalling is not my game. I would rather keep moving than hide.
The people came out to see something real. Give them that and I will be grateful.
You call me a substitute. I am the one who turned up when you did not.
You are proud of your {strength}. Fair enough. I respect that. Fair enough, honestly. I have a lot of respect for that.
I have been thinking about your {strength}. I want to find a way round it, honestly.
You stayed level, I am jealous. That is easy to say, so I will show you it is true in the ring.
Right, that is fair, I think. I think we both want the same thing from this.
I could be sharp, but I would rather be honest. I am choosing to be honest instead.
One fall, honest. Honest, simple, and I will give you everything I have.
On the mat I will be honest with you. I am not going to hide anything.
Grounded or standing, I am still going to try my best.
Stay where you are if you want. I will meet you in the middle.
That was a good answer. I mean that, and I think you know I do.
You have not answered yet. I will be patient, I promise.
Fair point, I am sorry. I will take it, and I will say so in the ring.
I take that on board. It is the right way to look at it.
I am going to give this everything I have until the bell goes.
My plan is simple: be honest and do the work properly.
Whatever happens, I hope you know I meant every word.
It is not decided yet. I am still hoping for the chance.
There is one more thing I want to say, and then I will get on with it.
Honestly, I've got no example that proves what I said. I'm sorry. I'd rather be fair to you.
I think I've made a mistake there. I can't establish the charge and I shouldn't keep pressing it.
Thanks. I think that's a much fairer way to start the match.
That's all right. Let's put that behind us and give it everything.
I'd like them to see how I get on when something I've practised doesn't go to plan. Honestly, that's enough.
We can find out whether I can hold my own against you. I'm happy to let the match answer that.
I don't know whether that accusation is true. What can we honestly show them when we wrestle?
Right, I'll try to put this simply. What can the people find out by watching our match?
Honestly, I am glad you've taken my {strength} seriously. I still get a chance to use them, don't I?
Right, you know about my {strength}. I am hoping I can make your answer a little harder to put into practice.
Oh, right. Sorry, I made that sound more certain than it is.
Fair point. I'd rather admit that now than keep repeating something I don't know.
I know you've had more time to learn things. I'm hoping to show you something you haven't had to answer yet.
Right, I won't argue with your experience. I would just like the chance to find out what mine is worth against it.
Honestly, having been through a few difficult exchanges helps me keep thinking when the first idea goes wrong.
I still get things wrong, but experience has taught me not to give up on a move the moment it gets awkward.
Right, you've watched me get that wrong before. I've actually been working on it, so I'd like another chance.
I know you've done your homework. Honestly, I've got a couple of new answers I'd quite like to try.
I study the moment I start to panic in a hold. Then I practise getting my feet back under me.
I've been rehearsing what to do after a failed entry. It feels a bit less like improvising in a crisis now.
